extracted.intended_audience: applicants for utility model registration, patent attorneys, national IP offices, inventors, employers and employees
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural, substantive and administrative rules governing filing, examination, grant, publication, transfer, licensing (including non-voluntary licenses), and employee-invention ownership for utility models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ownership of employee inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an invention is made by an employee in the execution of his duties or using the employer's material, tools or data, the employer has the right to be granted ownership or enjoyment of all or part of the rights attaching to the certificate protecting the invention; otherwise, all other inventions shall belong to the employee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The employee shall secure a fair price; if parties do not agree the competent domestic court shall fix it, taking into consideration evidence from employer and employee, initial contribution of each party, and industrial/commercial utility of the invention. Applies to employees of the State and public bodies, subject to national rules for supplementary remuneration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employee duty to inform employer
rubrics_metrics.description: An employee who makes an invention shall immediately inform his employer, who shall acknowledge receipt of the information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Immediate notification is mandatory to allow employer to assert rights under the Annex.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to share information and preserve confidentiality
rubrics_metrics.description: The employee and employer shall share all useful information on the invention and shall refrain from any disclosure that may partly or wholly jeopardize the exercise of the rights conferred by this Annex.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both parties must cooperate and avoid disclosures that could harm patent/utility model protection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agreements on employee inventions must be written
rubrics_metrics.description: Any agreement between the employee and his employer pertaining to an employee invention shall, on pain of invalidity, be recorded in writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Oral or informal arrangements are invalid; formal written contracts are required for enforceability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employer waiver transfers rights to employee
rubrics_metrics.description: If the employer expressly waives the right to the patent in the situation where employer would otherwise have rights, the right shall belong to the employee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Waiver must be express; in that case ownership shifts to the inventor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Client ownership for commissioned utility models
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless otherwise provided in the contract, the right to the certificate of registration of a utility model made in fulfillment of an order shall belong to the client.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default rule: commissioned works vest with client unless contract states otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations/exclusions to utility model rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Rights deriving from the utility model shall not encompass: (a) acts relating to objects offered for sale in Member State territory by the owner or with his consent; (b) use of objects on board foreign aircraft, land vehicles or ships temporarily or accidentally in Member State territory; (c) acts for experimental purposes in scientific/technical research or educational purposes; (d) acts by any person who in good faith on the filing date (or priority date) was in possession of the utility model.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are explicit exceptions limiting the exclusivity of the utility model owner; prior possessors have a right that may only be assigned with the attached business/goodwill.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment of prior possessor's right limited to business goodwill
rubrics_metrics.description: The right of the possessor referred to (good faith possession on filing/priority date) may only be assigned with the goodwill, business or company or the part thereof to which it is attached.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Possessor's rights are tied to the business context and cannot be separately assigned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing authority and compliance with Agreement/implementing regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: The application for registration of a utility model shall be filed with the Organization or the Ministry responsible for industrial property, in accordance with Article 8 of the Agreement, this Annex and the procedures set forth in the implementing regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must follow the competent filing office and any implementing regulations; noncompliance may affect admissibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required contents of utility model application
rubrics_metrics.description: The application file shall contain: (a) an application addressed to the Director-General; (b) proof of payment of requisite fees; (c) an unstamped private power of attorney if represented by an agent; (d) a sealed envelope containing: (i) a specification stating configuration/arrangement/mechanism set out clearly and completely so a person skilled in the art could carry out the model; (ii) necessary drawings/photographs; (iii) a descriptive abstract summarizing the specification; (iv) the claim(s) defining the scope of protection sought, not exceeding contents of the specification; (v) sufficient indications regarding best manner of carrying out the invention known to the inventor on the filing date (and priority date if claimed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All listed parts are mandatory; claims must not exceed the specification; the specification must enable a person skilled in the art to carry out the invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity of utility model — single principal subject and title
rubrics_metrics.description: The application shall be restricted to a single principal subject, with the details that constitute it and the uses specified; it shall contain no restrictions, conditions or reservations; it shall have a title describing precisely and succinctly the purpose of the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple unrelated inventions in one application are not permitted; title must be concise and precise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim of priority documentary and timing requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: To claim priority from an earlier application, the applicant must attach within six months a written declaration stating the date and number and country of the earlier application and applicant name; a certified true copy of the earlier application; and, if not the same person, a written authorization from the earlier applicant. Multiple priorities require separate compliance and fees. Failure to present any required document within the time limit entails loss of the priority benefit; documents received after six months are inadmissible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict six-month deadlines apply; fees must be paid for each priority claimed; missing documents mean automatic loss of priority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conversion rules between patent and utility model applications
rubrics_metrics.description: At any time prior to grant or rejection, a patent applicant may, on payment of the prescribed fee, convert to a utility model application (retaining original filing date), and vice versa; converted applications are deemed withdrawn in the original register; an application may not be converted more than once.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conversion preserves original filing date but counts as withdrawal of the original application; conversion is fee-dependent and limited to a single conversion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inadmissibility for non-payment of fees
rubrics_metrics.description: No application for registration of a utility model shall be admissible if it is not accompanied by a document attesting payment of the application and publication fees to the Organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof of fee payment is a threshold admissibility requirement; missing payment documents render the application inadmissible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing date requirements — documents needed at filing
rubrics_metrics.description: The Organization shall grant as the filing date the date of receipt of the application drafted in one of its working languages, provided that at the time of filing the application contains: (a) an express or implicit indication that grant of a certificate is sought; (b) information to establish the identity of the applicant; (c) a part which, prima facie, purports to be the description of an invention and one or more claims; and (d) proof of payment of the prescribed fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These minimal elements must be present at filing to secure a filing date; language of filing must be one of the Organization's working languages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication requirements and timeline for applications
rubrics_metrics.description: For each application the Organization shall publish: application number, filing date, applicant name and address, inventor name/address (unless inventor requested omission), agent name/address, statement of any priority(ies), priority date/country/number, title, abstract, date and number of international application (if any), and international patent classification symbols; the Organization shall also publish the specification, any claims and drawings (if applicable). The application shall be published within 18 months of filing or priority date (save for international applications).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publication is comprehensive and generally occurs at 18 months; certain items may be omitted for international applications as specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opposition grounds and procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Any interested party may oppose issuance of a certificate by sending within three months of the publication a written statement setting out reasons based on infringement of Articles 1,2,3,4 and 8 of this Annex, or of a prior registered right of the opposing party. The Organization sends the opposition to the applicant who may reply within three months (renewable once). The Organization may hear parties; if opposition is well-founded it may re-examine certain claims or terminate examination for all claims (or continue if groundless).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict three-month window for filing opposition; reply windows and possible hearing; outcomes include re-examination or termination of examination depending on grounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim of ownership procedure before Organization
rubrics_metrics.description: A person not entitled who files an application may be subject to an ownership claim by the entitled person within three months of publication, by written notice setting out grounds. The applicant may respond within three months (renewable once). The Organization shall hear parties on request; decision is appealable to the High Commission of Appeal within 60 days; Organization transfers application only if claim is well-founded and records final decision in its special register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ownership claims have defined timelines and appeal routes; Organization will only transfer applications upon well-founded claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Division/divisional applications — timing, priority, fees
rubrics_metrics.description: An initial application concerning several objects may be divided into divisional applications at least until issuance of the certificate, or during proceedings for examination, opposition, claim of ownership, and during appeals; divisional applications maintain the filing date and benefit of priority and require a fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Division preserves original filing date/priority but fees apply; permitted throughout most stages prior to grant or final decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination criteria and research report requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: An examination shall be conducted for all applications to establish: (a) the invention is not excluded under Article 4; (b) any claims are consistent with Article 11(2)(d)(iv) (claims not exceeding specification); and (c) provisions of Article 12 (unity) are met. A research report shall ascertain: whether at filing an earlier application for the same invention with older priority was in process of being granted; and whether the invention is new and industrially applicable. For PCT international applications the Organization may rely on PCT search and preliminary examination reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examination covers formal exclusions, claim consistency, unity, novelty and industrial applicability; international search/exam reports may be used for PCT cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant of certificate and disclaimers
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the Organization finds conditions for issuance met and the report prepared, it shall issue the certificate of registration of the utility model. Issuance is at the sole risk of applicants and without guarantee as to existence, novelty or merits of the invention, or fidelity/accuracy of the description. Certificates are issued by decision of the Director-General or authorized employee; certificates based on international applications include reference to international publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grant is administrative and not a guarantee of substantive patentability; applicants bear risk of challenges after grant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection procedure, correction period, and appeals
rubrics_metrics.description: Any application failing to comply with stipulations of Article 11 (except payment provision) and Article 12 shall be irregular and the applicant notified and invited to provide proper documents within three months (extendable by 30 days for justified necessity). An application regularized within the period maintains the initial filing date; failure to regularize leads to rejection. No application may be rejected if the applicant hasn't been invited to correct. Organization may correct obvious clerical errors. Applicant may appeal rejection to the High Commission of Appeal within 60 days; that Commission's decision is not appealable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formal defect notices and correction windows are mandatory before rejection; clerical corrections may be made by Organization; appeals limited to High Commission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certificates of addition — right to add improvements and formalities
rubrics_metrics.description: During the duration of the utility model, the inventor or successors have the right to make changes, improvements or additions by meeting formalities in Articles 11 and 13; such changes shall be attested by certificates of addition issued in the same form as the main certificate and have the same effect from their issuance date; certificates of addition taken by successors in title benefit all others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certificates of addition provide a formal route to protect post-grant improvements provided formal filing/formality rules are followed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Term and survival of certificates of addition
rubrics_metrics.description: Certificates of addition terminate with the main certificate of registration. However, invalidation of the main certificate does not automatically invalidate corresponding certificates of addition; they may survive until the normal term of the main certificate, subject to continued payment of annual fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additions may outlive main certificate in some circumstances but are subject to fee payments and legal conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conversion procedures for certificates of addition to main registration
rubrics_metrics.description: Provided a certificate of addition has not been granted, the applicant may convert his application for a certificate of addition into an application for a main certificate of registration; to obtain a main certificate instead of an addition the inventor must comply with the formalities in Articles 11 and 13.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conversion from addition-application to main application is permitted pre-grant, but main-application formalities still apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independence and mutual exclusivity of rights over related utility models
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person who has obtained a certificate of registration for a creation related to the subject matter of another utility model shall have no right to exploit the creation already protected and conversely the owner of an earlier certificate may not exploit the creation that is the subject of the new certificate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rights from different utility models relating to similar subject matter are independent and mutually exclusive with respect to exploitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication requirements for granted utility model certificates
rubrics_metrics.description: The Organization shall publish for each granted utility model: certificate number; filing number of application; filing date; applicant name and address; creator name and address (unless omitted by request); agent name/address; indication of any priorities; priority date/country/earlier application number; grant date; title; abstract; and international classification symbols. Implementing regulations determine procedures for publishing the model, drawings, claims and abstract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publication of granted registrations is thorough and controlled by implementing regulations for format and procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to descriptions, drawings and photographs — copies and requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Descriptions, drawings and photographs of registered utility models shall be kept at the Organization or, after publication, communicated on request. From publication any person may obtain official copies; applies also to official copies filed by applicants who claimed priority and to documents entitling applicants to claim priority. An applicant intending to avail priority before registration may obtain an official copy of his application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public access to patent documents is provided post-publication; priority-related documents are also accessible per rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transfer/assignment must be in writing
rubrics_metrics.description: Rights subsisting in an application or in a registered utility model shall be transferable in whole or in part. Acts involving transfer of ownership, licensing, assignment, pledge or cancellation relating to an application or registered utility model shall, on pain of invalidity, be evidenced in writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formal written documentation is required for transfer/licensing/assignment to be valid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration requirement for third-party binding and public record
rubrics_metrics.description: Acts referred to (transfer, license, assignment, pledge) shall not be binding on third parties unless entered in the special register of utility models and published in the Official Bulletin of Industrial Property; a copy of such acts shall be kept by the Organization. Subject to regulation, Organization shall furnish copies of register entries and certificates attesting absence of entries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public registration is necessary to affect third-party rights; register entries enable public notice and evidentiary copies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rights to benefit from improvements between owners and licensees
rubrics_metrics.description: Persons who have obtained from the owner or entitled persons the right to exploit the utility model shall benefit as of right from improvements made by the owner or entitled persons; conversely owner/entitled persons shall benefit from improvements subsequently made by persons who have obtained the right to exploit the model. Any person entitled to benefit may provide the Organization with a copy of the document attesting entitlement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mutual benefit from improvements is automatic among parties holding exploitation rights; entitlement documentation may be filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: License contract formalities, registration, and exclusivity rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The owner may grant a license by contract to exploit the registered utility model. The validity of the license may not be longer than that of the utility model. The contract shall be in writing and entered in the special register; it is not binding on third parties until entered and published per implementing regulations. The license may be removed from the register upon proof of expiry or termination. Unless otherwise provided, grant of a license does not preclude licensor from granting other licenses or exploiting the model; grant of an exclusive license precludes the licensor from granting other licenses and, absent contrary provisions, from working the model himself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formality and registration rules affect third-party binding; exclusivity requires clear contract terms and affects licensor's rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invalid and allowed clauses in license contracts
rubrics_metrics.description: Clauses in license contracts are invalid insofar as they constitute anti-competitive practices or impose restrictions on the licensee not deriving from rights conferred by the certificate or not necessary for upholding such rights. Exceptions not considered restrictions include: (a) restrictions relating to extent, scope or duration of exploitation; and (b) obligation on licensee to abstain from acts likely to impair validity. Unless otherwise stipulated, license is not assignable and licensee not authorized to grant sublicenses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: License clauses must not introduce anti-competitive or extraneous restrictions; customary operational restrictions are permitted; default assignability/sublicense limits apply unless contract states otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judicial ascertainment of invalid license clauses
rubrics_metrics.description: A civil court may ascertain invalid clauses in license contracts at the request of any person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties may seek judicial relief to have improper contractual clauses declared invalid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for non-voluntary (compulsory) license for non-working
rubrics_metrics.description: At request after four years from filing or three years from issuance (whichever later), a non-voluntary license may be granted where: (a) the utility model is not being worked on Member State territory at time of request; (b) working does not meet demand for the protected product on reasonable terms; or (c) refusal to grant licenses on reasonable commercial terms unfairly and substantially prejudices establishment or development of industrial/commercial activities. A non-voluntary license may not be granted if the holder provides legitimate reasons for non-working.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Time thresholds apply; grounds include non-use, insufficient use, and refusal to license on reasonable terms; legitimate reasons (e.g., regulatory or other acceptable causes) can bar compulsory licensing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compulsory license for dependent certificates — additional conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an invention protected by a certificate cannot be worked without infringing an earlier certificate and the earlier owner refuses authorization on reasonable terms, the owner of the later certificate may obtain a non-voluntary license if: (a) the later invention represents substantial technical progress of considerable economic interest relative to the earlier invention; (b) the owner of the earlier certificate has the right to a reciprocal license on reasonable terms; and (c) the use authorized relating to the earlier certificate shall be unassignable save where the later certificate is also assigned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dependent-certificate compulsory licensing requires demonstration of substantial technical progress and reciprocal rights; limitations on assignability apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application requirements and jurisdiction for non-voluntary license requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications for non-voluntary licenses shall be made to the competent domestic court of the domicile of the owner (or if domiciled abroad, civil court of elected domicile or place with agent). Only applicants domiciled in a Member State shall be considered. The application shall contain requester name/address; title and number of the certificate in respect of which license is requested; evidence that working does not meet demand on reasonable terms; and where applicable a statement undertaking to work the model on Member State territory to meet market needs. The request must be accompanied by proof that requester previously approached owner by registered letter for a contractual license and proof capability to work the model (for Articles 37/38).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Jurisdiction and standing restrictions apply (domicile requirement); documentary proof of prior attempts to obtain a license and capability to work are mandatory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Court procedure and decision contents for granting non-voluntary licenses
rubrics_metrics.description: The competent domestic court shall consider whether application satisfies requirements; if not, it shall reject but inform applicant of defects and allow corrections. If requirements satisfied, the court notifies owner and any licensees and invites written observations within three months, holds a hearing, and then decides to grant or refuse. If granted, the decision shall stipulate scope of license (acts covered and period; non-voluntary under Articles 37/38 may not include importation) and the amount of remuneration to be paid to the owner (equitable if parties fail to agree), subject to possible judicial revision. Decision shall be reasoned, transmitted to the Organization, entered in the special register and notified to licensees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural fairness includes notifications, observation windows, hearings; decisions must be reasoned and specify scope and remuneration, and are recorded publicly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rights and obligations of non-voluntary license holder
rubrics_metrics.description: After expiry of appeal time or after an appeal decision upholding the grant, the licensee is authorized to exploit the invention according to terms and must pay remuneration specified. Grant does not affect existing license contracts or other non-voluntary licenses and does not preclude other licenses, but the owner may not grant more favorable terms to others than those of the non-voluntary license.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-voluntary licensee derives enforceable exploitation rights but must adhere to terms and pay remuneration; owner is constrained from undercutting the licensee's terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations and transfer rules for non-voluntary licenses
rubrics_metrics.description: Beneficiary may not grant third-party permission to perform licensed acts without owner consent. A non-voluntary license may be transferred together with the goodwill/business working the invention, but such transfer requires competent domestic court authorization; the court shall afford the owner an opportunity to submit views, notify the Organization which shall register and publish the authorization; after authorized transfer the new beneficiary accepts same obligations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transfers of compulsory licenses are tightly controlled and require court authorization and registration; beneficiary's sublicensing rights are restricted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment and withdrawal of non-voluntary licenses and consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: On application by owner or beneficiary, the competent domestic court may amend the decision where new facts justify it. The court may withdraw the license on application by the owner if grounds for grant have ceased, beneficiary fails to comply with scope, or beneficiary is in arrears with payment. Withdrawal may be sought by other licensees in cases (a) and (b). If withdrawn because grounds ceased, beneficiary is allowed a reasonable period to cease working the invention to avoid serious adverse consequences. Articles 39 and 40 apply to amendment or withdrawal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-voluntary licenses are subject to ongoing supervision; withdrawal/amendment requires court process and may include transitional protections for beneficiaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals against non-voluntary license and other decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Within one month of publication, the owner, the beneficiary of a license, or any person who sought the grant may lodge an appeal with the competent higher court against specified decisions (granting non-voluntary license, authorization to transfer, amendment/withdrawal). The appeal has suspensive effect. Decision on appeal shall be notified to the Organization and entered in the special register and published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Short appeal windows (one month) and suspensive effect protect parties' rights; Organization is notified and records appeal outcomes.
